rounding: Brier scores to 9 decimals; squared-error sums, skills and expected scores to 6; percentages to 2; logarithmic scores and log-loss sums to 6 (natural logarithm); days to 3; 'exact' is the unrounded fraction

observed.unit: one forecast = two consecutive rows of one artifact, both with an effectiveness_to label

event: The effectiveness label of an artifact differs between two consecutive rows of its history (outcome 1 = changed, 0 = unchanged).

forecasters.kind: synthetic forecasters (assumed probabilities) scored on the observed pairs

never.description: States probability 0 of a change on every pair: PSY-005's persistence forecast, stated with certainty.

base_rate.description: States on every pair the share of all usable pairs that changed. That share is known only after every outcome has been seen: a hindsight forecast, used as the reference for skill.

one_percent.description: States probability 0.01 of a change on every pair.

five_percent.description: States probability 0.05 of a change on every pair.

coin.description: States probability 0.5 of a change on every pair.

long_step_hedge.description: Looks only at the earlier row of the pair: 0.1 when it is a seed row (the long step to the first feeder run), 0.001 otherwise. Both values were chosen by the author after seeing the data.

scores.brier_score: mean of (p - o)^2 over the pairs, o = 1 if the label changed
scores.log_score: mean of -ln(probability given to what happened); infinite if that probability is 0
scores.brier_skill: 1 - Brier score / Brier score of the base rate of the same set

one_pair.kind: computed; every forecaster keeps the probabilities it states on all pairs

proper_scoring.kind: synthetic: assumed true probabilities, closed-form expectations and a seeded sample
proper_scoring.definition: A scoring rule is proper when a forecaster's expected score is best if the stated probability equals the probability the forecaster believes.

formulas.expected_log_score: -t ln q - (1 - t) ln(1 - q), natural logarithm

hypothesis_check.kind: computed; the thresholds are those of the hypothesis in the research-cycle record
hypothesis_check.note: Two parts are identities and could not have failed: a constant forecast cannot beat the base rate of the set it is scored on, and -ln(0) is infinite. The spread and the share are the empirical parts.

worked_examples.kind: computed on the observed pairs (exercises 1, 2, 3 and 5) and synthetic (exercise 4)

transfer_task.note: Hypothetical release log for the learner task. Not Streeling data and not a forecast.
transfer_task.event: the release is rolled back within a day

checks.check: no stored logarithm is within 0.000001 of a rounding boundary of its last digit

no constant forecast has positive Brier skill against the base rate of the set it is scored on
no two forecasters tie in a ranking
